thought.text: I found that `uv sync` runs before `COPY . /app`, so the staged dirs aren't in the container yet. Now I'll check the Dockerfile ordering to confirm the sequence.

reasoning_content:
The stage directory has bizlog (816K) and decision-protocol (504K), but the context transfer was only 251.67 kB. Something excluded them.

The .dockerignore has `.pypirc`... no wait. What would exclude `bizlog/`? Looking at the patterns... `lib/` no... `parts/` no... `sdist/` no... `.env` no...

Wait — `*.egg-info/` no. Hmm, `.cache` — no, that's a file/directory name "cache" with a dot...

Ah, wait. The pattern is `var/` — no. Let me think: `bizlog/` — is there a pattern that matches "bizlog"? ... `build/` no. Hmm, `*.egg` — no, it's an exact name match with a wildcard.

Actually — the `.dockerignore` has `.venv` (without a trailing slash!). "Environments: .env, .envrc, .venv, env/, venv/, ENV/". `.venv` is an exact name match. Doesn't match bizlog.

Hmm, what about `dist/`? No. `parts/`? No.

Wait, maybe the context size is misleading: 251.67 kB is what was transferred after compression? BuildKit compresses the context! The transfer size is the compressed one. du -sh = 2.4M on disk; the compressed transfer is 251 kB? That seems like a very high compression ratio, but text (markdown, code) compresses really well (10:1 for text is possible). The previous dokumentenpruefung context was 1.87MB → transferred as "19.70kB"?? That was for a context of about 4MB or more. So the transfer size is the compressed one, and it's meaningless for determining exclusion.

So the context size doesn't tell us about the exclusion. The real problem: `/app/bizlog` doesn't exist inside the container at the time of RUN. But the stage has bizlog/. So either dockerignore excluded it, or... the RUN stage of the builder didn't receive it because COPY came later.

Look at the Dockerfile (line 18):
```
WORKDIR /app
RUN --mount=... uv sync --locked --no-install-project --no-dev
COPY . /app
```
This is the order! `uv sync` before `COPY . /app`. So at the time of uv sync, /app is empty — /app/bizlog doesn't exist yet, and not even the pyproject.toml that's the target of the bind mount exists?? The bind mount provides pyproject.toml and uv.lock. uv sync generates metadata for the editable project (the root) and needs the root project's pyproject.toml — provided by the bind mount. The path dependency bizlog needs to be at /app/bizlog — which should come from COPY — but that hasn't happened yet!

So, in the original monorepo layout, this pattern "worked"?? In the original: service directory = context root; bizlog is at ../../03-shared-services/bizlog (relative from /app) = outside the context → should have failed in the original too... unless the original build used the monorepo root as the context (in that case /app = the entire monorepo, and the COPY . /app before uv sync copies everything including 03-shared-services)? Let me re-check the actual Dockerfile order.
